Asha Patel: Quick question — who should own admin-level escape hatches for Private deployments? Ops is pushing for more runtime controls but Product wants API-level guarantees.
Ben Chu: Ops should own the runbook and the actual operator actions. Product should own the public contract (what we promise to customers) and the observability SLAs. We need a clear handoff doc.
Carmela Rivera: Agreed. In practice we hit three handover surfaces: config schema (what flags exist), auth/role mapping (who can invoke), and telemetry/audit (what we log). If any of those are fuzzy, oncall gets paged during a customer incident.
Asha Patel: Good call. Can we sketch a minimal contract in-thread? Something like: 1) Admin API = explicit opt-in per-tenant; 2) Runtime operator actions limited to a defined set; 3) Audit events emitted for every action.
Ben Chu: +1. Suggest we include exact event names and fields so downstream compliance teams can rely on them. Example minimal YAML for the runtime side:```yaml
admin_access:
  enabled: true
  roles: [infra-admin, sec-admin]
  allowed_actions: [force-fallback, drain-queue, evacuate-tenant]
  require_2fa: true
```
Lee Morgan: One nuance: in Dedicated we may allow `evacuate-tenant` but in Hosted we must `force-fallback` to a cheaper model first. The contract should list behavior per hosting mode, not a single catch-all.
Patrick O'Neill: Ops note — evacuate-tenant is destructive. We need a soft path: `quiesce` -> `migrate-cached-state` -> `evacuate`. Add rate-limited triggers and a safety TTL.
Carmela Rivera: Also call out the auth mapping: customer-admin vs redwood-operator. Who signs the final KMS envelope when doing cross-tenant data movement in Private? We should never assume central key access.
Asha Patel: Right — Private: customer KMS only. Dedicated: customer-managed keys optional. Hosted: Redwood KMS. Add these as explicit lines in the contract.
Ben Chu: Oncall ergonomics: add a playbook step for every admin action that includes required audit tags and link to the rollback snippet (one-liner). Example rollback: `redwoodctl restore-tenant --from-backup <id>`.
deploy-bot: Deploy notice: `admin-handovers/v0.1` doc pushed to `docs/ops/hosting-handovers.md` (commit 8f3a2b).
Lee Morgan: Nice. Can we list owners and SLA for the doc? Ops owns maintenance, Product owns review. Review cadence: quarterly.
Patrick O'Neill: I'll put an RFC in the backlog and link ENG-2409. Actionables: Patrick to author RFC skeleton; Ben to draft YAML contract examples; Asha to coordinate product review with compliance.
Carmela Rivera: One more thing — add a small matrix for runtime fallback semantics: columns = Hosted/Dedicated/Private; rows = `low-memory`, `kernel-oom`, `degraded-kv`. Define whether we `fallback`, `retry`, `evacuate`, or `quiesce`.
Asha Patel: Great. If everyone agrees I can turn this thread into a short doc and assign owners. :thumbsup:
Ben Chu: :thumbsup: fine by me.
Lee Morgan: :+1:
Patrick O'Neill: I'll create ENG-2409 today and link the doc.
Carmela Rivera: Thanks — this should cut down on late-night surprises for oncall.
